Residual old-body anchors remain: criterion 14 'tip peak speed not below the baseline (18.3 m/s)', where the baseline speed comes from a wrist servo at its limit in 92–100% of steps (gap map row 7). reads.abandoned_worth_revisiting:
1. Prototype '나' (SIMBICON-like: hip rights the pelvis, foot placement, human torque budget on engine motors too). It was best on the human-limit column (26/30 scenes under the limit, walking hip 183/242 N·m) but lost the base choice on a single-run function count of 35 vs 20 (physics2_proto_round1 §3; patch docs/strike/physics2_proto/simbicon.patch).
2. Gait branch A (pre-planned footsteps). It was dropped on a longsword-only 85 vs 103 of 144. B turned out to be longsword-tuned (254/432, rapier and zweihander walking 0/8), and A was never measured on three weapons (digest 16:38 and 16:56).

reads.patterns:
The measuring tool was handled well. Criteria were written before results, the noise floor was measured and banded, share metrics were dropped when their denominator misbehaved, the yaw threshold was traced to an engine friction mechanism, and requested torque was replaced by delivered torque. Most of this came through audit cross-checks.

The errors gathered in the fast loop of build rounds and in what was reported to the owner:
(a) Small or single-condition samples decided choices: single-run 35/41, longsword-only 103/144, 8-bout fight cells of ±2 bodies, and an unverified definition table.
(b) Battery classifiers passed a different motion (reqlunge counted a passing step). Rising pass totals were reported as progress while fights and the real move set lagged (D, acknowledged twice in the records).
(c) Old-body parity crept back in after the criteria disowned it. Rule 15 said fight falls are 'a different body', but later gates require never-fell bodies near the anchored current game. Battery scenes and thresholds are admitted or set by what the current game does (run 5 m/s, a front-foot lunge from a walk). Leg strength was decoupled to keep 'the old game's meaning', which the record says came from the hidden support.
(d) The human-muscle half of the goal (나-8) stopped being reported once the honesty rows passed. The one number on record, walking hip peak 690–746 N·m, is about 3× the limit.
(e) Designs consistent by construction (GRF within joint limits, double support while cutting, strict aid definition, honest get-up, the human-budgeted '나') were dropped on pass counts near noise or under time pressure after the owner's 16:43 remark, while external aid sized like the old anchor (yaw 100) was added to approach old-game fight numbers.

Most of the lead's verdicts that went wrong were self-corrected within hours. The uncorrected ones are the yardstick choices (c) and the unreported human-limit check (d).

reads.patterns:
1. Old-body parity was used as the target whenever a timing or rate existed in the shipped game. Examples: the walking lunge's 0.1–0.25 s, 'steered distance at least half the game's', the finishing-thrust 61 %, and battery thresholds re-tuned until the propped game passes (kick2 raised to 100 N·s because the anchor kept the game's foot down). Where the target was physical (the 5 m/s run, gathered-step timing from fencing), the work was opened and the conclusions held up.
2. Old snapshot tests were read as motion damage: the ±5 % motion_regress (kote included) and 'N of 982 broken'. This was reported to the owner first and classified later. Even after atkdef_diag showed 21 of 34 were fixed values, the round4 §0 conclusion was not amended, and the 23:23 '15 due to the setting' count again used old tests as the damage measure. This leads straight into the 11/26 'fewest old tests changed' arm choice.
3. n=8 gate cells decided rejections (fast lunge), and a 'two attempts and stop' rule was added. The records themselves say single cells flip by ±1–2 and fights need 96 games. Owner reports sometimes carried face-value deltas (40 → 46 'worse') while the verifier called them noise.
4. Counter-pattern, done well: the lead and workers repeatedly chose correct-by-construction over numbers (defect fixes kept despite 40 → 53 falls; biglunge kept as a true lunge; no running push), separated seen from unseen seeds in the round-5 verdict, retracted a guessed cause within minutes, and put the legs in the owner's hands. The owner's hands-on 'more realistic' and the score-based 'cannot ship / wall' disagreed. That disagreement is the clearest sign in this period that the yardstick, not the physics, was what fell short.
5. The solver-iteration finding is an example of the forest: the old game aims correctly only because two errors cancel. In this period it was still framed as 'attack must be at iteration 1 to be right', with parity targets (54 %, 0.08 m, 17 → 0 tests) carried into 11/26.

Beyond the two cases already acknowledged (kote, fewest-tests), the same habit shows up in three more ways this period.
- Counts of old repo tests were used as targets and costs from the start: '깨진 시험 17 → 0' was a design target, '35 깨진 채' was counted against the new legs in the self-assessment, and the 5-vs-2 test count decided the S2 choice. - Raw success counts were read without opening the denominator or noise: Zweihander parries that include non-threats; 'self-falls' that include contact-driven falls; a single-instant onset-phase classifier.
The causal diagnoses themselves (trunk ruled out, solver identified, rope cause found) were done well, by opening joints and running causal experiments. The error came at the verdict and selection step, where opened evidence was then outweighed by unopened counts measured against the old body.

challenge.refuted:
1) Stage-0 numbers (5 m/s median, 'muscles ×10'), 2) the gap-map 'sword is not slow', 3) the round-2 'external righting torque is not the answer': each was a real slip, but the records show it was corrected within hours (h3 §3-2, digest 01:23 and 16:56, round2 §8-4), and no lasting decision rested on it. They are history, not live errors.
4) Decoupling leg strength from proficiency (q10): the stated reason was old-game parity, but the alternative was not more correct. A real adult at 65 % strength still walks well above 0.7 m/s, so the slowdown under 'multiply' is a weakness of the controller, not physics. The fight numbers (4.88 vs 2.78 self-falls/min) also favour decoupling.
5) Legs-notes design (a), GRF matched to joint limits: both variants keep torque within human limits, so (a) is not more physically correct. Its loss was also beyond noise (rapier walk 8 → 3; −97 on the 0.65 set). Design (c), shortening requested steps, was not clearly more correct either. Design (b), deferral, stands (see above).
6) Rejecting the fast front-foot lunge (r4_req §5-1): the gate count was flawed, but the rejection also rested on real falls (1 in 4 runs, w_lunge45 0/24, d_lunge6 2 of 4). Reviving it would chase the old game's timing, which is the very error flagged in the 'wall' item. The gathered-step lunge is the correct route and it worked in round 5.
7) Engine kept (17:27): the main reason was the cost of a rebuild. The arm/leg solver conflict the reviewers wanted re-tested was later shown to be an arm-calculation bug (aim at the tight solver 77 %), not an engine artifact.
8) The 12:09 self-assessment as a separate error: its counter-quote from main_entry §3 was itself retracted at 16:0x. Opened up, the 35 broken tests include real gaps (run 1.7 m/s, Japanese stance 0.071 m, clinch, pommel strike), so counting them was not purely an old-body yardstick. The 7.5 % out-of-range figure was reported in the same message (line 1845). The parts that hold (fall row, rebuild booked as waste) are covered by the fall-classifier and S2 items.
9) Round 5 candidate (a), pre-bracing for the sword reaction: reactFF already counters the reaction within the same step, and the unmet residual was small, so the decision did not rest on the onset classifier alone. Only (c) stands.
10) The aid-definition table being 'unverified': ② was re-run on the final code at 45/96 (legs_notes line 235). Only ① is unconfirmed.
challenge.revive:
In order of value to the goal:
(1) B2 rope-arc arm as the arm base (already ordered at 15:41/15:45), with two-hand arms under the upper-arm twist limit: lift the 10/24 bull-tap exemption and re-author that thrust instead.
(2) Prototype '나''s engine-motor human-torque budget (docs/strike/physics2_proto/simbicon.patch), or s5's exact-force Rapier 0.21 path. This is the only route recorded so far to legs that are within human muscle by construction.
(3) Cut-time step deferral (double support during the cut, legs_notes §2-4 and §4-2), as the physical replacement for the 100 N·m yaw aid.
(4) Tool fix 2's physical-outcome scenes (standcatch, wretreat, humancut), and drop the copied-from-game thresholds.
(5) Gait branch A, measured on three weapons.
(6) Cheap leftovers: balance-first (r4_balance §4-2), the unloaded-foot filter with the never-tried >0.1 s rule (§4-4), F1 'start walking on stick intent' (atkdef_diag §9; its two broken tests were pinned values and were never traced), and the honest get-up (src/getup.js, diagnosed as 'sequencing, not force').
Do not revive the fast front-foot lunge.
challenge.pattern: The measuring tools themselves were usually built well, and the causes, once opened, were found correctly: delivered torque, the yaw friction mechanism, the solver, the rope. The error that keeps coming back sits at the verdict and selection step. Whenever the shipped game had a number for something (a fall count, a wound %, a lunge timing, a scene pass, a pinned test value), that number became the target or the cost. This happened even though the records themselves said the number came from the hidden support, the anchor or two errors cancelling. The gap was then reported to the owner before anyone opened it ('worsened', 'wall', 'cannot ship', 'kote half as long'). Separately, the property that defines the project, legs within human muscle (나-8), quietly stopped being measured once the pass rates began to rise. In short, the team measured how closely the new body copies the old one, when the goal was a body that obeys physics. The legs that the scores called 'not shippable' were the ones the owner, playing them, found more realistic.
